title: Replying to @The Play Bill Chronicles it’s holy, hilarious, and heali...
transcript: Remove every connotation you have about the word Ho, cause in Ho church, we are reclaiming it. Brandon Kyle Goodman defines Ho as someone who's committed to liberating themselves and others by interrogating their relationship to shame, love, and pleasure with communication, curiosity, and compassion. And that is exactly what Ho Church does. I grew up Jewish, and I've never felt comfortable in a church until now. But Brandon creates a space that feels both divine and spiritual, but also deeply silly and playful. It's a mix of Mr. Rogers Neighborhood and Dr. Ruth. There's puppets and learning and DJ Ari grooves, but also pain and truth and real collective vulnerability. Won't always feel comfortable, but in the best way, because Ho Church pushes conversations we've always been told to avoid around queerness, faith, sex, and shame. And yet it always feels safe, like you're being held like you're exactly where you're supposed to be. And it's such a testament to the community Brandon builds throughout the show. They are the kind of preacher we all need right now. Compassionate, fierce, and so funny. Truly, if every service felt like this, I would go to church every single week.
